segments.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Before we get going, I'd like to confirm what we agreed by emails. I'm using this meeting's transcript to write up your requirements, and the AI that helps me with that runs on my own computer, so nothing leaves it. Is everyone still happy with that?
Yes, that's fine. Fine by me. Yes, I'm happy with that.
Thank you. Ayanda, I think your camera has frozen, but I can hear you.
Sorry, it's the school Wi-Fi. It's always like this after two o'clock when the boarders come back.
No problems. So, Lindiwe, you wrote
that parents are struggling to get information from the school. Tell me more of...

Yeah, right now, everything goes out on paper or by email from school base. Fee statements are printed every month and sent home in the learner's bags, and half of them never reach the parents. Then I have parents phoning me about fees they didn't know they owed.
And reports are the same. Printed, put in envelopes, sent home. For about 900 learners, that's a week of the admin staff's time every term.
And notices, like sports fixtures or a school closure.
Those go on WhatsApp broadcast lists and by email. But a broadcast list fills up, so we have five of them now, and parents who change their numbers just fall off.

And absence notes. Handwritten in the learner's homework diary or an email to the class teacher, who may or may not pass it on to the office. We had a learner marked absent for three days last term, and nobody at the office knew why.
That sounds stressful for everyone. So what's the main thing you want out of this?
One place where a parent can see what they owe, their child's reports, and the school's notices, and tell us when their child is sick.
And for us to stop printing, that's a real cost in a lot of hours.
Let me take those one at a times. Fee statements first. What would a parent need to see?

The current balance. The monthly statement as a PDF. And the reference to use for EFT. We don't take card payments, and we're not going to. So there's no paying through the portal. Parents pay by EFT or debit order, like now.
Got it no payments in the portal. And the reports.
The term report as a PDF, the same when we print, released on the same day for everyone. We don't want some families seeing them before others.

That day is the problem. When reports come out, every parent logs in within a couple of hours, mostly in the evening. We've got about 1,400 parent contacts. Last year we put one grade's reports on the website as a test, and the site fell over.
That's useful to know. And the notices?
Notices from the office and from the grade heads, either to the whole school or just to one grade or one team.
And absence notes a parent fills in a form.
Yes, the reason and the dates, and the class teacher and the office both see it straight away.
Now school base. Where does it run? On
a server in the admin block. It's school base 7, from about 2014, I think. It holds the learners, the parents' fees, and marks. It can export to CSV, and it produces the report PDFs.
Does it have any kind of APIs?
Not that I know of. I've asked the supplier, and they haven't answered yet.
Then it's an open question, how the portal gets fresh data. One option I'd suggest is a nightly CSV export from school base that the portal picks up, so we never touch school base itself.
Um, I'd want to know how out of date the balances would be. Parents pay on the first, and phone me on the second. Let's talk about it once we've heard from the supplier.
Fair enough. What about the parents' phones and data?

Most of our parents have smartphones, but data is expensive, and I'd say most of them are on prepaid. I think most parents would use the portal on their phones rather than a computer, but honestly, we'd need to check. We've never asked them.
Our bursary families especially count every megabyte.
So the portal has to be light, small pages, and the PDFs only downloaded when someone actually opens one.
Yes, and could it be zero-rated? I heard some schools have arranged that with the networks.
That I'd have to look into. I'll note it as a question.

On security, I want to be very clear. These are children's records. Reports, the medical reasons on absence notes family addresses. Only a learner's own parents or guardians may see anything about that learner.
And with some divorced parents, one of them may not see anything at all. There's a court order on about a dozen files.
That's an important one. So the portal has to respect restrictions per parent, and the office has to be able to set them. Yes,
exactly.
And does the data have to stay in South Africa?
The board said it must be hosted in South Africa. That came out of the last board meeting.
Okay. What about language and accessibility?
English is the school's language, but a lot of our grandparents look after the children, and they're more comfortable in Issy Zulu.
If the notices and the main screens could be in Issy Zulu too, that would mean a lot.
And big, clear text. Some of our parents struggle with their eyesight, and we have a blind parent on the PTA who uses a screen reader. Oh, and please use the school's maroon, not some generic blue.
Noted. And the budget. The finance
committee has proposed 250,000 rand for the first year all in, but the board has to approve it, and they only meet on the 28th of January.
Then we'd want a firm figure ready for that meeting. And timing, when would you want it working?
The term two reports go out on the 26th of June. We'd like parents to get those through the portal.
Ayanda, I've just looked in school base while we were talking. It's not 1,400 parent contacts. It's about 1,650. A lot of families have both parents and a grandparent listed.
Thanks, 1,650, then. A risk I see is that if the first report day goes badly, parents lose trust in the portal straight away. I'd suggest a trial with one grade's term one reports first.
I like that. Let's do grade 8 in April as the trial.
Agreed. Grade 8 first.
Any risks from your side that I should know about?
Me, honestly. I'm the only IT person, and only two days a week. If something breaks on report night, there's nobody.
That's an honest answer. Thank you. Anything you'd want later, but not in the first version.
Eventually, booking slots for parents'
evenings. But not now.
Good. I'll send the summary and the open questions by Friday. Thank you all for your time.
